previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for increased green, blood-streaked tracheal secretions, dyspnea, substernal burning, and subjective fevers. She was evaluated for possible tracheitis or pneumonia. A bronchoscopy revealed erythema and suspicious plaques; cultures grew Moraxella catarrhalis and a pan-sensitive gram-negative rod (Proteus). She was treated with oral levofloxacin for presumed bacterial tracheitis. Her symptoms improved with antibiotics, nebulized bronchodilators, and supportive care. GERD and depression were managed with home medications. Iron supplementation was discontinued as her anemia remained stable. She was discharged home with follow-up instructions and a five-day course of antibiotics.
problems: Obstructive chronic bronchitis with acute bronchitis
